statement: Feedback loops and runaway agent behaviour
description: This risk arises when an agent repeatedly acts on its own outputs, or agents reinforce each other’s decisions, outputs, or errors, with no bound on how many steps it takes, how much it spends, or how far its actions reach. As a result, feedback loops may form that escalate actions, consume excessive resources, or cause the system to persist in harmful or unintended behaviour without effective human intervention.

controls.statement: Grant agents only the minimum permissions required for their designated tasks
Limit the scope of agent actions through predefined thresholds and baselines
Ensure every agent can be immediately paused or terminated by its operators
Implement circuit breakers to prevent cascading failures in multi-agent systems
